target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.
